mainTopic: Craftsmen and items in their hands: רבה's ruling on a craftsman's חזקה is refuted, utensils switched at a craftsman's shop, and the craftsman who refuses to show a cloak.
overview: רבה had ruled that a craftsman has no חזקה only when there are עדים that the item was handed to him. Without such עדים, he is believed if he says the item is his. The גמרא tries to support רבה from a ברייתא about a craftsman arguing over his fee. That proof is pushed off: the ברייתא may be talking about a case where the owner never saw the item with him. Then רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks רבה from the teaching 'אומן אין לו חזקה'. The גמרא agrees this is a true תיובתא, so רבה's ruling falls. Next, a ברייתא teaches that utensils switched at a craftsman's shop may be used, but utensils switched at a house of mourning or a feast may not. רב explains the reason in his uncle's name: people often ask a craftsman to sell their items. רב חייא בריה דרב נחמן limits this to a case where the craftsman himself handed over the utensils and said 'a cloak,' not 'your cloak.' Finally, אביי shows רבא how a craftsman in פומבדיתא denies having a cloak and then refuses to show it. רבא answers that the craftsman's claim is fair, and his reason comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the proof for רבה from the craftsman's fee
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be a case without עדים. Since the craftsman is believed about his fee because he could have claimed he bought the item, this supports רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the case one where there are no witnesses? And it teaches that the craftsman is believed. Since he could have said 'I bought it, that's why it's in my hands,' he is also believed about his wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof for רבה. It says the ברייתא about the craftsman's fee must be talking about a case with no עדים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The craftsman is believed about his pay because of a מיגו: he could have made a stronger claim, 'I bought it.' That stronger claim only works if there are no עדים that he got the item as a job. So the ברייתא seems to show that without עדים a craftsman can claim ownership, which is exactly רבה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': a person is believed on one claim because he could have made a better claim and been believed
A craftsman who works on other people's items
Is it not? (introduces the conclusion the גמרא is pushing for)

steps.confusionAlert: The craftsman is NOT actually claiming the item is his. He only wants more pay. The גמרא is pointing out that he could have claimed ownership, and that is why his smaller claim about the fee is accepted.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not where there are no witnesses?
And it teaches: the craftsman is believed,
since if he wanted, he could have said to him:
'It is bought, and that is why it is in my hand,'
he is believed also about his wages!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun before this section, where the גמרא brought the ברייתא about the craftsman's fee and asked what case it is talking about.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that without עדים a craftsman is believed to say the item is his.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a craftsman holding the item is believed about his fee, based on a מיגו of 'I bought it.'

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: the owner never saw the item with him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really is a case without עדים, but it is also a case where the owner did not see the item in the craftsman's hands. So it does not prove רבה's broader ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It really is a case with no witnesses, but it is a case where the owner did not see the item with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for רבה. It limits the ברייתא to a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees there are no עדים, but adds another detail: the owner never saw the item with the craftsman. Then the craftsman could have denied ever receiving it, so of course he is believed. That does not prove רבה's ruling, which believes the craftsman even when the item was seen in his hands. The proof is gone, but רבה has not been disproven yet.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really' or 'actually': keeps the earlier assumption while adding a new detail
And that is when he did not see

phrases.english: No, really it is where there are no witnesses,
and it is where he did not see.
phrases.notes: 'He' means the owner. He never saw his item sitting with the craftsman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבה's ruling itself still stands for now.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא covers every case without עדים. In fact it may cover only the case where the owner did not see the item with the craftsman.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק reads the teaching 'אומן אין לו חזקה' closely
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes 'a craftsman has no חזקה' and draws an inference: only a craftsman has none, but someone else would have a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects: 'A craftsman has no חזקה.' It is a craftsman who has no חזקה, which means another person does have a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק opens an attack on רבה. In this step he is only setting up an inference from the wording; the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching singles out the craftsman. That suggests that an ordinary person in the same situation would have a חזקה. Next, the גמרא will ask what case this could be, and that answer will cause the problem for רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumption of ownership based on possessing an item
'But then': introduces an inference from the wording
Another person, someone who is not a craftsman

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak raises an objection:
A craftsman has no presumption of ownership.
It is a craftsman who has no presumption,
but another person does have a presumption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רבה fell away, a new attack against רבה begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that without עדים a craftsman has a חזקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up an inference from the wording: an ordinary person does have a חזקה. The attack itself is completed in the next step.

steps.title: The case must be without עדים, so רבה is refuted
steps.stepSummary: If there were עדים, even another person would have no חזקה. So the teaching must be about a case without עדים, and still a craftsman has no חזקה. This contradicts רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If there are witnesses, why would another person have a חזקה? Rather, isn't it a case with no witnesses? And it teaches that a craftsman has no חזקה. This is a refutation of רבה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's attack. It shows that the teaching must be about a case with no עדים, which goes against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עדים that the item was given to him, nobody could claim it as his own. So the 'another person has a חזקה' case must be without עדים. That means the craftsman also lacks a חזקה even without עדים, which is the opposite of what רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
A refutation, a strong challenge from a source

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one inference from the wording ('only a craftsman') can knock down an אמורא's ruling once the גמרא pins down the case.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If there are witnesses,
phrases.notes: Witnesses that the item was handed to this person to hold or to fix.

phrases.english: why would another person have a presumption?
Rather, is it not where there are no witnesses?
And it teaches: a craftsman has no presumption.
This is a refutation of Rabba!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the inference of step 3 by fixing the case as one without עדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teaching must be about a case without עדים, yet it says the craftsman has no חזקה. רבה said a craftsman does have one in that case.

steps.title: The refutation stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: it is a true refutation of רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and does not defend רבה. His ruling is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A one-word 'תיובתא' at the end means no answer was found. In the end, a craftsman has no חזקה on items he holds, even when there are no עדים that they were given to him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה said that without עדים a craftsman is believed to say an item is his. The proof for him was pushed off, and the teaching 'אומן אין לו חזקה' refuted him completely.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.
phrases.notes: The repeated word means the גמרא agrees: no answer, so רבה's view falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the refutation raised in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה is refuted. A craftsman has no חזקה even without עדים.

steps.title: Switched utensils: craftsman's shop versus mourning house or feast
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that utensils switched at a craftsman's shop may be used. Utensils switched at a house of mourning or a feast may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If someone's utensils got switched with another person's utensils at a craftsman's shop, he may use them until the other person comes to take his own. But if they got switched at a house of mourning or at a feast, he may not use them until the other person comes to take his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא with two cases of mixed-up utensils that get opposite rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases a person ends up holding someone else's utensils by mistake. At the craftsman's shop he may use them while he waits. At a mourning house or a feast he must leave them alone. The ברייתא does not explain the difference, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: They got switched or mixed up
A house of a feast, such as a wedding

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If his utensils were switched with other utensils
in the craftsman's shop
this person may use them,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא הַלָּה וְיִטּוֹל אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: until that other one comes and takes his own.
phrases.notes: הַלָּה means 'that other guy.' He is the real owner of the utensils this person ended up with.

phrases.english: In a house of mourning or in a house of a feast
this person may not use them,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא הַלָּה וְיִטּוֹל אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: until that other one comes and takes his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִתְחַלְּפוּ לוֹ כֵּלִים בְּכֵלִים בְּבֵית הָאוּמָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new craftsman-related topic after the refutation of רבה in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Utensils switched at a craftsman's shop may be used in the meantime. Utensils switched at a mourning house or a feast may not.

steps.title: Why the two cases differ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes the first case different from the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא allows using the utensils in the first case but not in the second. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases look the same: someone holds another person's utensils by mistake. So there must be some reason the craftsman's shop is special. The גמרא wants that reason spelled out.

phrases.english: What is different about the first clause
and what is different about the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the two different rulings of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason using the utensils is allowed at a craftsman's shop but not at a mourning house or a feast.

steps.title: People sometimes ask a craftsman to sell their item
steps.stepSummary: רב reports his uncle's answer: a person often tells a craftsman to sell his item, so what the craftsman hands over may be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: I was sitting before my uncle, and he said to me: Isn't a person likely to tell the craftsman, 'Sell my cloak for me'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the answer he heard from his uncle. A craftsman's shop is a place where owners sometimes leave items to be sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a craftsman's shop, the item may have reached you through the craftsman with the owner's permission, since owners sometimes tell the craftsman to sell their things. That possibility makes it allowed to use the item. At a mourning house or a feast nobody handed anything over with permission. It is just a plain mix-up, so you may not use someone else's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'my beloved one.' This is רב's name for his uncle, רבי חייא

phrases.english: Rav said:
I was sitting before my uncle,
phrases.notes: חַבִּיבִי literally means 'my beloved one.' רב calls his uncle רבי חייא by this name.

phrases.english: and he said to me:
And is a person not likely
to say to the craftsman, "Sell my cloak for me"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲוָה יָתֵיבְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּחַבִּיבִי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Owners commonly ask a craftsman to sell their items, so an item handed over by the craftsman may have been given with permission. A mix-up at a mourning house or a feast has no such possibility.

steps.title: Only when the craftsman himself handed it over
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב נחמן limits the היתר to a case where the craftsman himself handed over the utensils, not his wife or children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בריה דרב נחמן said: They taught this only when he himself gave it, but if his wife and children gave it, no.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows the ruling of the ברייתא. You may use the utensils only if the craftsman personally gave them to you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning in step 8 depends on the craftsman knowing which items he was told to sell. His wife or children do not know those arrangements. When they hand something over, it is most likely just a mistake, so using it is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of: introduces a limitation

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya son of Rav Nachman said:
They taught this only about him himself,
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the craftsman himself handed over the utensils.

phrases.english: but his wife and children: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא הוּא, אֲבָל אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו – לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of the ברייתא based on the reasoning of step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using switched utensils is allowed only when the craftsman personally handed them over.

steps.title: Only when he said 'a cloak,' not 'your cloak'
steps.stepSummary: Even when the craftsman himself hands it over, using it is allowed only if he said 'a cloak.' If he said 'your cloak,' he clearly made a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even with him, we said this only when he told him 'a cloak' without specifying. But if he said 'your cloak,' no, because this is not his cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בריה דרב נחמן adds a second limitation: it depends on the craftsman's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the craftsman says 'here is a cloak,' it could be a replacement he was allowed to give. If he says 'here is your cloak,' he thinks it belongs to you. Since it does not, this is clearly a mistake, and you may not use it.
steps.whatToRemember: At a craftsman's shop you may use switched utensils only if the craftsman himself gave them and he called it 'a cloak,' not 'your cloak.' At a mourning house or a feast you may never use them.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'your cloak' sounds like it gives more permission, but it is the opposite. It proves the craftsman was mistaken, because the cloak is not yours.

phrases.english: And even him,
we said this only where he said to him:
"a cloak" without specifying,
but "your cloak": no,
this is not his cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהוּא נָמֵי – לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, further limitation on top of step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even from the craftsman himself, use is allowed only if he said 'a cloak.' If he said 'your cloak,' it is clearly a mistake.

steps.title: The trick of the swindlers of פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows רבא how a dishonest craftsman denies having an owner's cloak and then refuses to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: Come, I'll show you what the swindlers of פומבדיתא do. The owner said, 'Give me my cloak.' The craftsman answered, 'This never happened.' The owner said, 'But I have witnesses who saw it with you!' The craftsman said, 'That was a different one.' The owner said, 'Bring it out and let's look at it!' The craftsman said, 'Actually, I'm not bringing it out.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells a short story that shows a typical trick of dishonest craftsmen in פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the craftsman denies ever getting the cloak. When witnesses say they saw it with him, he switches his story and says it was a different cloak. When the owner asks to see it, he refuses. אביי calls this a trick, but רבא will disagree in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: These things never happened: a complete denial

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
Come, I will show you
the swindlers of Pumbedita, what they do.
He said to him: "Give me my cloak."
phrases.notes: Here the owner is talking to the craftsman.

phrases.english: "These things never happened."
phrases.notes: Now the craftsman answers and denies he ever got the cloak.

phrases.english: "But I have witnesses
who saw it with you!"
He said to him: "That was a different one."
"Bring it out and let us see it!"
He said to him: "In truth, I will not bring it out."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: תָּא אַחְוִי לָךְ רַמָּאֵי דְפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new craftsman-related teaching about a dishonest craftsman's tactics.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The swindlers' trick is to deny the cloak, then say it was a different one, then refuse to bring it out to be examined.

steps.title: רבא says the craftsman has a fair claim
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers אביי that the craftsman who refuses to show the item is making a reasonable claim. His explanation will follow in the coming lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He (the craftsman) is speaking properly to him (the owner).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's suspicion and says the craftsman's claim is a fair one. This is a setup line, and the גמרא is about to give his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, אביי made the craftsman's refusal to show the cloak look like proof that he was dishonest. רבא says the refusal does not have to be a sign of lying, because the craftsman's words make sense. Why they make sense is what the next line will explain.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבא finishing his point. He has only said that the craftsman is right, and the explanation is still coming.

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: He is answering אביי, who just showed him the craftsman's behavior in step 11.

phrases.english: He is speaking properly to him –
phrases.notes: "He" is the craftsman and "him" is the owner of the cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא responds to אביי's demonstration in step 11 by defending the craftsman's claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The craftsman's claim to the owner is a valid one. The reason follows in the next line.
